mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the case weight plus the end-of-arm tool, and for multi-case picks, the combined weight of the cases. How a case behaves when cold also affects gripping. TRF validates the final payload with your product, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach, and the table above shows the typical case weight for each platform.

mainEntity.name: How Does a Robotic Palletizer Handle SKU or Pallet Pattern Changeovers?

acceptedAnswer.text: A changeover usually means selecting a stored recipe that holds the case dimensions, pick logic and pallet pattern for the new SKU. When the new case fits the same end-of-arm tool, the change happens mostly in software. TRFCobot and TRFCompact store multiple recipes and pallet patterns, so a SKU change does not mean rebuilding the process.

mainEntity.name: Who Makes Robotic Case Palletizers With Local Support in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF Industrial Automation designs, builds, installs and supports robotic palletizers for manufacturers across the United States, from the collaborative TRFCobot to TRFSubzero for areas below 32°F.
